official.deadline_note: The binding earlier date is the Master's programme application: VU advises applying for admission no later than 1 December 2026, because you can only apply for the VUFP after you have been conditionally admitted, and admission decisions take 4-6 weeks. General programme deadlines are 1 April 2027 (non-EU/EEA needing a visa) and 1 June 2027 (EU/EEA and others not needing a study visa).
official.application_cycle: 2027/2028 cycle (September 2027 intake); VUFP application open from 1 November 2026, results expected mid-March 2027
official.status_note: The official page heads the call 'Call to apply: 1st November 2026' and states 'Applications are welcome from November 1st 2026', so the round for the September 2027 intake opens in November 2026 and closes 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET).
official.tuition_coverage_note: The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only. It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances. Be aware that you must be able to finance these living expenses by yourself.
benefits: VU Amsterdam has committed to providing approximately 1 million euros towards attracting highly motivated and excellent students.
The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only. It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances.
When applying for the VUFP scholarship, you automatically also apply for the NL Scholarship (formerly HSP) as well. No separate application is necessary.
NL Scholarship is a one time contribution towards the costs of living of EUR 5,000 for the entire duration of your study period, awarded only for the first year.
We have around 20-25 NL Scholarships available per year. Only a few of the VUFP awardees will get the NL Scholarship.

As one of our most excellent students, you agree to become an international student ambassador during your studies at VU Amsterdam, answering questions from prospective students through the Unibuddy chat platform.
eligibility: You hold a non-EU/EEA passport and you are not eligible for the lower tuition fee.
You do not have the Dutch nationality.
You can prove your academic excellence (GPA equivalent to a Dutch 8).
You are conditionally or unconditionally admitted to the first year of a full-time English-taught Master's programme at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam starting per September 2027.
Students starting in February cannot apply; joint programmes where VU Amsterdam does not administer the admission process are excluded from VUFP.

The degree with which you are seeking admission has not been obtained in the Netherlands, you do not have a degree from an education institution in the Netherlands, and you are not currently enrolled in a Bachelor or Master programme in the Netherlands.
You do not need to complete a preparatory programme before the start of your Master.
Students already enrolled in a two-year Master's programme who have not been awarded the VUFP scholarship in 2026/2027 are not eligible to apply for the VUFP scholarship for 2027/2028.

Applicants who previously completed a semester or full academic year at VU Amsterdam via the Semester in Amsterdam programme are covered by the standard procedure, with one VUFP reserved for that group.
requirements: Excellence in previous (bachelor) education is proven if the grade point average achieved is at least equivalent to the Dutch grade of an 8.0 on the Dutch grading scale 1-10.
You do not need to convert your grades to the Dutch ones. The VUFP Scholarship Committee will do that by deciding on the local grade equivalents for the Dutch grade of an 8.0.
Even if you have already completed a Master's degree, for VUFP application purposes, we will look only at your GPA from your bachelor's degree.
Please note that you can apply for the VUFP only for one Master's programme.
Please note that you can submit your application only once. Make sure to double check if your application is complete and sufficient before submitting it. You will not be allowed to submit it again.
Applicants for an English-taught Master's programme must meet the English language proficiency requirements, unless exempt.
A scholarship granted for one academic year cannot be postponed to another academic year.
documents: The VUFP-NLS application form (Application form 2027-2028) - older versions of the application form will not be accepted
GPA proof / programme transcript showing your most up-to-date grades, pasted at the end of the form
A grading scale explanation with a clear explanation of the GPA calculation
The completed form saved as one file in .PDF format and uploaded in the Scholarship section of the personal VU dashboard
Bachelor's degree transcript and grading scale of your bachelor's degree
Programme application documents in PDF format, including the VU Application Form template (for the admission stage)

English proficiency evidence: accepted test results (IELTS Academic, TOEFL iBT, Cambridge C1 Advanced/CAE or C2 Proficiency/CPE, LanguageCert Academic, Pearson PTE Academic, or the VU-test) or proof of an exemption
selection_criteria: The selection process considers three main criteria: academic quality of students, the quality of the study program, and the comparison amongst all applicants, maintaining each student's anonymity.

All VUFP applications received by 1 February 2027 (23:59 CET) will be reviewed by the faculty of the applied for Master's programme. Faculties will then nominate applicants to the Central Scholarship Committee, which will subsequently award scholarships to the most talented students.
The results will be based on the academic performance and motivation.
Other factors (such as your motivation for this university/specific programme, future ambitions, extracurricular activities, etc.) also play a significant part in the scoring process.
Meeting the minimum GPA requirement is only a minimum that should be reached so we accept and process your application, and is by no means a guarantee to actually be offered the VUFP Scholarship.
The total score used to rank all applicants is based on several factors, of which GPA is only one.
coverage: The VUFP scholarship covers the tuition fees only.
It does not provide any additional allowance towards study or living costs, like rent, food, insurances. Be aware that you must be able to finance these living expenses by yourself.

The waiver equals the applicant's programme-specific institutional (non-EEA) tuition fee; VU's published 2027-2028 institutional Master fee schedule for non-EEA students ranges from EUR 6,500 to EUR 39,120 per year, with EUR 25,370 and EUR 24,970 the most common rates.
NL Scholarship is a contribution towards the costs of living of EUR 5,000 for the entire duration of your study period, awarded only for the first year of your study programme.
The VUFP can be granted for a one- or two-year Master's programme; the scholarship will only be extended for the second year if 100% of the ECTS during the first year have been achieved.
application_method: Step 1: Register for a Master's programme (from 1 October 2026) in Studielink and complete it in your personal dashboard on vu.nl. You must have been already conditionally admitted to the Master's programme before you can apply for the VUFP scholarship. Advised deadline Master's programme application: 1 December 2026.

Step 2: Submit the VUFP application (from 1 November 2026) in your personal VU dashboard. To apply, fill out the VUFP-NLS application form. Older versions of the application form will not be accepted.

At the end of the form, paste the GPA proof/programme transcript and a grading scale explanation. Once done, save it as a one file in .PDF format and upload it in the Scholarship section of your personal dashboard on vu.nl (located on the Complete Registration page).

To be considered complete, the application form must include all the answers and the GPA proof / programme transcript. Not answering one or more questions or not including the GPA proof / programme transcript will result in your application being considered incomplete and therefore not evaluated.
Step 3: Decision. The Central VUFP Committee decides which students will be offered a VUFP scholarship. Faculties nominate applicants to the Central Scholarship Committee.
Step 4: Results. All students will receive an e-mail/notification informing them of the Central Scholarship Committee's decision. Expected date: mid-March 2027 (6 weeks after the deadline).

Step 5: Acceptance. Selected candidates accept/decline the VUFP and NL Scholarship offer in their personal VU dashboard. Deadline to accept the offer when selected: end of March 2027 (2 weeks after the results have been published). If you do not take action within 2 weeks after receiving the results, the offer will be withdrawn.
official.application_route: Apply for the Master's programme in Studielink and complete it in the VU dashboard, obtain conditional admission, then submit the single VUFP-NLS application form PDF once in the Scholarship section of the personal VU dashboard by 1 February 2027.
official.study_mode: full-time (the programme must be a full-time English-taught Master's)
official.citizenship_residency: You must hold a non-EU/EEA passport, not be eligible for the lower tuition fee, and not have the Dutch nationality. Dutch degree holders and applicants to joint programmes VU Amsterdam does not administer are excluded.
official.international_eligibility: Open only to non-EU/EEA nationals who pay the higher institutional tuition fee; EU/EEA students and Dutch nationals are not eligible. Students from Suriname and Switzerland are additionally not eligible for the accompanying NL Scholarship because they pay the lower (statutory) tuition fee.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Any full-time English-taught Master's programme at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam starting September 2027, with two exclusions: students starting in February cannot apply, and joint programmes where VU Amsterdam does not administer the admission process are excluded.
official.duration: One or two years, matching the Master's programme duration; the scholarship is only extended for the second year of a two-year Master's programme if 100% of the ECTS during the first year have been achieved
official.description: The VU Fellowship Programme (VUFP) offers talented prospective non-EU/EEA students the unique opportunity to pursue a Master's degree at Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam, with VU Amsterdam having committed to providing approximately 1 million euros towards attracting highly motivated and excellent students. It is a merit-based tuition fee waiver covering tuition fees only, with no allowance towards study or living costs. Applying for the VUFP automatically also enters the applicant for the NL Scholarship.
official.program_type: Merit-based tuition fee waiver for incoming non-EU/EEA Master's students
official.english_requirement: Applicants to English-taught Master's programmes must demonstrate sufficient English language proficiency, either automatically based on previous fully English-taught education, by completing an accepted test (IELTS Academic - online/Indicator/One Skill Retake not accepted; TOEFL iBT - Home Edition, Essentials and MyBestScore not accepted; Cambridge C1 Advanced/CAE or C2 Proficiency/CPE; LanguageCert Academic; Pearson PTE Academic; or the VU-test offered by the VU Taalloket, EUR 150, not accepted by the School of Humanities and School of Theology), or by a granted formal exemption. Tests must be no more than two years old before 1 September of the start year; exact required scores are published per programme in VU's official English Language Proficiency Overview 2027-2028.

not_confirmed: funding_amount: no single euro figure per awardee is published. VUFP waives the programme-specific institutional (non-EEA) tuition fee; the published 2027-2028 fee schedule for non-EEA Master's students spans EUR 6,500 to EUR 39,120 per year (most commonly EUR 25,370 / EUR 24,970), so the value depends entirely on the programme admitted to.
travel_coverage: not covered and not itemised beyond the statement that the VUFP provides no allowance for study or living costs such as rent, food and insurance.
Number of VUFP awards granted per cycle: not published; only the overall approximately EUR 1 million commitment and the separate figure of around 20-25 NL Scholarships are stated.
Exact per-programme minimum English test scores: published only in VU's separate 'English Language Proficiency Overview 2027-2028' PDF, not on the scholarship page itself.

Whether the NL Scholarship is EUR 5,000 or EUR 10,000 for a given applicant: the scholarship page states EUR 5,000 as a one-time contribution, while the VUFP Terms and Conditions PDF states 'EUR 5,000 EUR or EUR 10,000'; the master's-level figure published on the page is EUR 5,000.
verification.notes: All figures taken from VU Amsterdam's own scholarship page, the official VUFP 27-28 Terms and Conditions PDF and the official 2027-2028 institutional tuition fee schedule; cross-checked against the VU Master's application and English language requirement pages. Deadline, eligibility, coverage limits and procedure confirmed verbatim. No aggregator sources used.

applicant_utility.summary: VUFP is a tuition waiver rather than a stipend: it removes the non-EEA institutional tuition fee for one full-time English-taught Master's at VU Amsterdam and leaves rent, food, insurance and travel entirely on you. Entry is a two-stage funnel in which the December 2026 programme-application date matters more than the February scholarship deadline, because the VUFP form only unlocks once you hold a conditional admission. The same single form also enters you for the EUR 5,000 NL Scholarship, but with only around 20-25 of those per year and a different selection procedure, it should be treated as a bonus rather than a funding pillar. Treat the GPA bar as a filter, not a ticket: only a small slice of foreign grade distributions clears the Dutch-8 equivalent, and the top applicants are ranked on motivation, ambitions and extracurriculars on top of grades.
applicant_utility.best_fit: A non-EU/EEA applicant with a top-decile bachelor record (Dutch-8 equivalent) targeting a full-time English-taught Master's at VU Amsterdam who can self-fund roughly EUR 12,000-18,000 per year of Amsterdam living costs.
application_readiness_checklist: Start the Master's programme application in Studielink and the VU dashboard in October 2026, aiming for 1 December 2026 rather than 1 February - conditional admission is a hard precondition for the VUFP.

Confirm the fee you will be charged is the institutional non-EEA rate and look up your programme's exact figure on VU's 2027-2028 institutional fee schedule, so you know the euro value of the waiver before you apply.
Download the current 'Application form 2027-2028.docx' from the scholarship page; VU explicitly rejects older versions.

Merge everything into ONE PDF before uploading: form answers, GPA proof/programme transcript, and a written grading-scale explanation - an unanswered question or missing transcript is classified 'incomplete' and is not evaluated at all.
Verify your bachelor degree was not obtained in the Netherlands and that you are not currently enrolled in a Dutch Bachelor or Master programme.
Rule out the deal-breakers early: no February start, and no joint programme where VU Amsterdam does not run the admissions.
Plan to accept or decline in the dashboard within two weeks of the mid-March result, and diarise the 31 August 2027 enrolment and tuition-payment cut-off.
common_rejection_risks: Submitting the VUFP form before conditional admission - the application simply cannot be made, and there is no workaround.
A blank question or a missing transcript/grading-scale note: the file is deemed incomplete and is not evaluated, with no chance to resubmit.
Assuming 8/10, 80% or 3.2/4.0 automatically equals a Dutch 8 - VU converts by grade distribution statistics via ECCTIS, so naive conversions usually fall short.
Applying for the VUFP for more than one Master's programme; only one is permitted even if you hold several admission offers.
Targeting a February intake or a joint programme VU does not administer.
Being a continuing two-year Master's student who was not awarded VUFP in 2026/2027 - that cohort is explicitly barred from the 2027/2028 round.
Missing the two-week acceptance window after the mid-March result, which automatically withdraws the offer.
Losing the second year of the waiver by earning less than 100% of first-year ECTS.
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Living costs are explicitly excluded from the VUFP and must be self-financed: Amsterdam rent, food, health and liability insurance, plus the EUR 100 non-refundable application fee, visa/residence-permit costs and flights. Add any programme-specific institutional tuition that the waiver might not reach in full, and for a two-year programme remember the second year is conditional on earning 100% of first-year ECTS. The NL Scholarship, if won, offsets only the first year with EUR 5,000.
document_audit: The form must be the 2027-2028 version; VU states older versions will not be accepted, so ignore any cached copy saved last cycle.
One single PDF only - do not upload the transcript and grading scale as separate attachments.
You never convert your own grades; the VUFP Scholarship Committee decides local equivalents for a Dutch 8.0, but you must still supply a grading-scale explanation so they can.
If you have not yet graduated, an up-to-date transcript or GPA proof is sufficient - you do not need the final diploma at this stage.
Only the bachelor GPA is assessed, even for applicants who already hold a Master's degree; sending a Master's transcript instead wastes the single submission.

English test results can follow later, but scores must be shared through the provider system (IELTS TRF number, TOEFL institution code 7947, LanguageCert/PTE/Cambridge sharing) or VU cannot verify them.
alerts: The real gate is the 1 December 2026 advised programme-application date, not the 1 February scholarship deadline - admission takes 4-6 weeks and you cannot apply for the VUFP without it.
One submission only; an incomplete file is not evaluated and cannot be corrected.
The NL Scholarship is automatic but scarce: around 20-25 awards, only a few VUFP recipients receive it, it covers the first year only, and Suriname and Switzerland nationals are excluded from it.
A scholarship granted for one academic year cannot be postponed to another academic year.
Enrolment must be fully completed and tuition fees paid before 31 August 2027, or you cannot start on 1 September 2027.
Holders take on an international student ambassador role for the whole Master's (Unibuddy chats plus an October kick-off session), which is a condition of holding the award.
VU assesses no scores sent by email or in advance of the application period - only a complete submitted application is reviewed.
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Studielink registration plus VU dashboard programme application by 1 December 2026, then conditional admission, then a single one-shot VUFP-NLS form PDF with transcript and grading scale merged in, uploaded once in the Scholarship section of the VU dashboard by 1 February 2027 23:59 CET, followed by faculty review, Central Scholarship Committee nomination, a mid-March result and a two-week acceptance window in the dashboard.
